# 31_parse_manuscript.sh - Markdown version of the manuscript

<!-- BEGIN pipeline-callers: generated by tools/automation_doc_links.py, do not edit by hand -->
:::{attention} Usually run by a Bitbucket pipeline
`31_parse_manuscript.sh` is normally not run on its own. The Bitbucket pipelines listed below call it as one step of a longer job, after earlier steps have prepared its inputs and environment. Run it by hand mainly for debugging or local testing.

## Description

Downloads the PDF attachments of the Jira ticket into a scratch directory, converts the manuscript(s) with [manuscript_to_markdown.py](#help-manuscript_to_markdown), commits the result as `manuscript_parsed/` through `20_commit_code.sh` (no tag), and pushes it with [32_pull_push.sh](#help-32_pull_push) in `rebase` mode. The PDFs themselves are not committed here; `30_download_commit_jira_attachments.sh` does that.

The pipeline runs alongside the ingest, which pushes to the same branch. `manuscript_parsed/` does not overlap anything the ingest touches, so whichever pushes second just pulls the other's commit first. Before pushing, the script restores `generated/` to its committed state, because the log that `20_commit_code.sh` writes there would otherwise block the rebase.

After a successful conversion, the script also commits the checksums of the manuscript(s) as `generated/manuscript.sha256`, the only file this pipeline pushes under `generated/`. [33_trigger_parse_manuscript.sh](#help-33_trigger_parse_manuscript) uses them to skip this pipeline when the manuscript has not changed. The script itself does not check them, so running the pipeline by hand always converts the manuscript. A failed conversion records nothing, so the next ingest tries again.

If the checksums are missing or differ, the script removes `manuscript_parsed/` before converting, so that nothing from an earlier manuscript, such as its figures, remains next to the new result. The earlier result stays on the branch if the conversion fails or if no manuscript is attached.

## Usage

```bash
. ./tools/resolve_jiraticket.sh
./automations/31_parse_manuscript.sh
```

### Environment Variables

- `jiraticket` - Required; set by `tools/resolve_jiraticket.sh`.
- `JIRA_USERNAME`, `JIRA_API_KEY` - Required for the attachment download.
- `BITBUCKET_BRANCH` - Branch to push to (default: the current branch).

With no manuscript among the attachments, the script reports that and exits 0 without committing.

See the [m-parse-manuscript pipeline](#pipeline-m-parse-manuscript), which runs it.
